status: first form (roadmap 14.2, docs/campaign/03_THE_BATTERY_MISSION.md section 1); the fronts' triggers (track F, F4.4)
notes: The 15th SAM Regiment's tasking of a battery (simcore/campaign/regiment.hpp): each rule a trigger the regiment can know, the task, and the reason the order gives. Routine rules are read at the evening briefing, urgent ones at once. The regiment knows the enemy's picture of the battery only from our intelligence's estimate in the campaign's journal; the fronts (F4.4: the covered division's withdrawal, its sector's priority, the sky's sharing there) only from what reached its commander or its staff through the pipeline, read only where the ground war and our air defence commanders run (ground.mode and ad_strategy.mode 1).
source: voenizdat_osa_1991 pp. 232-239 (a battery changes position only on the regiment commander's order; reserve positions within 2 km); docs/campaign/03_THE_BATTERY_MISSION.md section 1 (the rule table)

officer.source: sam3d estimate (Lt Col Josef Vrana, data/command/chain_pannonia.json: a class 1 regiment commander, a little bolder than the book; the traits as data/campaign/ad_strategy.json's commanders have them, trait_shift its 0.2)
officer.notes: Track O, O7: how readily the regiment's commander leaves the textbook. His willingness, 0.5 + trait_shift x (boldness + creativity - rigidity - methodical), scales each rule's departure: a rule's score is its adversary's weight x (1 - departure x (1 - willingness)), and it fires at its threshold (0.5 unless given). The textbook's rules have departure 0.

rules.reason: The bridges are first on the division's priority list and have no low cover.
rules.source: docs/campaign/03_THE_BATTERY_MISSION.md section 1 (an object on the priority list without low cover: cover it); docs/command/05_PLACES.md section 3 (routine tasks at the 19:00 briefing); sam3d estimate (the object: the campaign's)
rules.notes: First form: one object for battery 21. The division's priority list and the regiment's other batteries come with 13.8 and the five batteries.

rules.reason: Our intelligence estimates the enemy has found your position.
rules.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 pp. 232-239 (the change of position by the regiment's order, to a reserve position prepared within 2 km); docs/campaign/03_THE_BATTERY_MISSION.md section 1 (the trigger and the reason); sam3d estimate (ready_in_s: the commander's short sequence, about 12 min; the march under 2 km with the vehicles out of their emplacements and the column closed up, about 20 min; the post's 18 min occupation, data/campaign/battery_plan.json; with a margin)
rules.notes: Each estimate moves the battery once, and only an estimate made after the battery reached the position it holds; the old main position becomes a reserve.

rules.reason: The division withdraws to its next line; the regiment moves its batteries back with it so that its troops stay covered.
rules.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p. 238 (a battery changes position only on the regiment commander's order) and pp. 234-238 (a battery in defence 3-5 km behind the forward edge, 1.5-3 km from the troops it covers, kept so as the line moves: docs/fronts/04_AIR_DEFENCE_STRATEGY.md section 4); vr_poltikovic_1984 p. 96 (the division's 3-4 prepared positions, its lines 6-8 km apart: back_m the near end); sam3d estimate (work_s: the regiment commander's decision on the order or report and its words on the net by the duty officer, about the army's chief of air defence's own half hour; ready_in_s: the commander's short sequence, about 12 min, a march of 10-20 km at a column's 20-30 km/h by day with its halts, about an hour, the post's 18 min occupation, data/campaign/battery_plan.json, and a margin)
rules.notes: Track F, F4.4: on what reached the regiment's commander or its staff of the covered division (the 7th Motor Rifle Division, the 15th SAM Regiment's: the ground feed's withdrawal and relief orders and its reports that it has withdrawn), each withdrawal once. The battery goes to the nearest of its prepared positions (data/command/places_pannonia.json bty21_depth_*) at least back_m further behind the front's line than its main position; an object's cover becomes a relocation from there, troops' cover stays theirs.

rules.readiness_text: no. 1 throughout: the division's sector has the main thrust
rules.reason: The army's chief of air defence has raised the division's sector to defend: the main thrust is there.
rules.source: docs/fronts/04_AIR_DEFENCE_STRATEGY.md sections 2 and 4 (the army's chief of air defence's priority by sector; the regiment takes his priorities and covers the main thrust); andersen_1979 p. 40 (60 % of the air defence to the main thrust); sam3d estimate (readiness no. 1 throughout for a battery on the main thrust; work_s as withdraw_with_division's; ready_in_s: the battery at its position, the order and its readiness checks)
rules.notes: Track F, F4.4: an order of the army's chief of air defence (campaign/ad_strategy.hpp, F4.1) on the division's sector that reached the regiment's commander, each once; the battery keeps its task and position (the regiment's other batteries and the moves to the main thrust come with its five batteries).

rules.readiness_text: no. 2, no. 1 on the regiment's warning: the division's sector is quiet
rules.reason: The army's chief of air defence has put the division's sector to economy: no thrust there.
rules.source: docs/fronts/04_AIR_DEFENCE_STRATEGY.md sections 2 and 4 (economy: a quiet sector, what remains of the air defence, at least one fire unit in each object's cover); sam3d estimate (readiness no. 2 for a battery in a quiet sector; routine, at the evening briefing)
rules.notes: Track F, F4.4: as sector_raised_to_defend, read at the regiment's evening briefing.

rules.reason: The sky's sharing in the division's sector has changed.
rules.source: vr_krupicka_1984 pp. 62-64 (the sky shared by zones or in one zone by height, the method set by the PVOS formation's commander; the SAM troops and the fighters each told the other's); data/command/own_air.json sky_by_sector (the method by the sector's priority, F4.3); sam3d estimate (work_s: the regiment's duty officer passes it on)
rules.notes: Track F, F4.4: the method for the division's sector by the national sector's commander's priority there, as the orders that reached the regiment's commander give it (his pre-war plan before any), told when it differs from the plan of cooperation the battery holds; heard at the battery's post, the plan is shared that way (ScenarioRunner::RegimentTellsSharing).

rules.reason: The regiment trusts your battery's reports: your launchers search and fire on their own in their sectors.
rules.source: docs/campaign/12_ORDERS_MAPS_AND_THE_CAMPAIGN.md sections 3 (D6: trust decides who gets the important task) and 7 (track O, O5); pvo_bu_ix_1984 (search and fire on the senior commander's designation, or independently); sam3d estimate (the bands: an excellent day and the trust above its prior of 0.8, data/gameplay/after_action.json)
rules.notes: Track O, O5: read at the evening briefing, once per summing up, on the standing the regiment holds from the battery's records (simcore/campaign/grading.hpp): the task held, its launchers on their own (the harder task, and more of the battery's own judgement).

rules.reason: Your battery's reports have not held up: your launchers fire on your designation only.
rules.source: docs/campaign/12_ORDERS_MAPS_AND_THE_CAMPAIGN.md sections 3 (D6) and 7 (track O, O5); pvo_bu_ix_1984 (search and fire on the senior commander's designation); sam3d estimate (the bands: an unsatisfactory day, or the trust under 0.7, data/gameplay/after_action.json's grade_3)
rules.notes: Track O, O5: as trusted_on_its_own; a battery the regiment cannot believe is held on a short rein: its launchers on its commander's designation only.

rules.task_text: the covered division is broken: withdraw with its remnants to the next line, fighting on your own on the way
rules.short_ru: отходить с остатками дивизии, действовать самостоятельно
rules.reason: The covered division has been broken and dispersed: the battery must not be left alone in front of the enemy.
rules.source: vr_1980_krizek_encirclement pp. 37-42 (cut off: the senior officer there commands all units; leaving in small groups without the equipment is inadmissible; air defence goes with the breakout); vr_poltikovic_1984 p. 96 (the division's lines 6-8 km apart: back_m); sam3d estimate (work_s, ready_in_s as withdraw_with_division's, quicker on the regiment's side)
rules.notes: Track O, O7 (docs/campaign/12 section 8, situation 3): on the covered division's Dispersed order as it reached the regiment, each once; the textbook (departure 0).

rules.reason: The regiment's radars are all off the air: the battery fights on its own, roving between its positions.
rules.source: pvo_bu_ix_1984 (search on the senior commander's designation or independently; sudden targets engaged independently and reported after); vr_1985_plss (a gap in the picture means autonomous combat); sam3d estimate (the regiment's standing order, given before as the battery's instruction for this case: work_s, ready_in_s)
rules.notes: Track O, O7 (situation 7, contact lost): every radar of the regiment's the battery follows off the air, once per outage. Given in person beforehand as a standing instruction, so it reaches the battery without the net it lost.

rules.reason: The loan is over: back to your task.
rules.source: sam3d estimate (a temporary task ends at its hours; the task held before it is given back at the evening briefing)
rules.notes: Track O, O7: for the rules with lasts_h (a launcher detached for an object, an ambush).

rules.reason: Your battery has been in line long enough and is short of missiles: the reserve battery relieves you.
rules.source: vr_1982_volny_ad_restoration pp. 52-59 (a weakened system restored by moving units from depth and from less important directions, missiles shifted, repairs by priority; but 'we usually form no SAM reserves', p. 54: both recorded, the regiment's reserve battery is sam3d's); sam3d estimate (days_in_line, missiles_below: half a battery's 16 ready; rest_h; ready_in_s: the handover and the march to the rear)
rules.notes: Track O, O7 (situation 2, rotation): on the battery's own ready report (its missiles as it said them), once per report. The reserve's column goes on the roads to the battery; once it is there it fights beside it and the battery marches to the rear, rests rest_h and is repaired and loaded.

rules.reason: The enemy's raids fall elsewhere: the regiment masses its fire units on the main direction.
rules.source: vr_1981_fanfule_army_ad_defence pp. 50-55 (the army's SAM regiment puts its emphasis on the enemy's main attack; batteries 10-15 km apart; it covers a first-echelon division lacking its own regiment); sam3d estimate (min_raids, ratio, window_h, near_m; work_s; ready_in_s: a march of some 20 km and the occupation; the weights: the masses of the Pact and NATO move more of our air defence than the rebels' raids)
rules.notes: Track O, O7 (situation 1): the raids reported by the warning net that reached the regiment in the window, away from the battery against near it; the battery goes to the prepared position nearest their middle. The textbook (departure 0).

rules.reason: An object near you has been struck again and again and has no cover: one launcher covers it for two days.
rules.source: vr_1982_volny_ad_restoration p. 58 (cover restored by moving fire units from less important directions); docs/campaign/12_ORDERS_MAPS_AND_THE_CAMPAIGN.md section 8 (a launcher detached: the senior man on the spot); sam3d estimate (min_raids, window_h, near_m, lasts_h, ready_in_s; departure: splitting a battery leaves the book; the weights: against small raids on many objects, more so)
rules.notes: Track O, O7: the object raided most often in the window away from the battery; the last sector's launcher (or the rule's vehicle) goes alone to the prepared place nearest it, deploys and fights on its own, its commander the senior man there.

rules.reason: The rebels' helicopters strike the villages and the roads: each launcher covers a village on its own.
rules.source: kuito_memoirs pp. 68, 92, 97-98, 300-301 (hindsight, Angola 1987-88: Osa round an airfield, Strela-10s split over a brigade's area and given singly to tactical groups; nothing on launchers singly over villages); sam3d estimate (the rule itself, min_raids, ratio, window_h, ready_in_s and departure: game values, never 1985 doctrine)
rules.notes: Track O, O7 (situation 4): against the rebels only (no weight for the others). Hindsight flagged: the cases are after 1985. The sectors' launchers go one to each village in order, fire independent.

rules.reason: The enemy's helicopters come in again and again by the same way: lie in ambush on it, radars silent.
rules.source: vr_1985_jurica_ad_on_the_move pp. 46-50 (fire ambushes and decoy firing positions); nhandan_2025_tan_bn61_1966 and sggp_2025_regt238_vinhlinh (Vietnam 1966, published 2025: the march kept secret, radio and radar only on order); sam3d estimate (min_raids, window_h, lasts_h, ready_in_s, departure and the weights)
rules.notes: Track O, O7 (situation 5): helicopter raids from one entry in the window; for a day, then the task held before.

rules.reason: The enemy strikes the country's power, fuel and dams: the regiment lends the battery to cover the dam for three days.
rules.source: vr_1985_jurica_ad_on_the_move pp. 46-50 (one zone-and-object defence with the national air defence under one command post); not found: a troops' battery lent to the national air defence (docs/research, R1); sam3d estimate (the rule's values and the weights)
rules.notes: Track O, O7 (situation 6): strategic objects raided away from the battery; a loan of lasts_h, then the task held before.

rules.reason: The army's chief of air defence has raised another division's sector to defend: the regiment sends you there.
rules.source: vr_1981_fanfule_army_ad_defence pp. 50-55 (the regiment goes over a first-echelon division lacking its own regiment or with heavy losses; it covers the second-echelon divisions); docs/fronts/04_AIR_DEFENCE_STRATEGY.md section 2; sam3d estimate (work_s, ready_in_s, weights)
rules.notes: Track O, O6's part 3: the army's chief of air defence's order raising another sector to defend, as it reached the regiment; the battery goes to its prepared position nearest that sector's middle.

rules.reason: The division's first echelon goes into the counterattack: cover its regiment, behind it on its axis.
rules.source: vr_1981_fanfule_army_ad_defence pp. 50-55 (the regiment ready in a counterstroke's area at least 1 h before it: ready_in_s); voenizdat_osa_1991 pp. 232-239 (the battery 1.5-3 km behind the covered companies); sam3d estimate (work_s, weights)
rules.notes: Track O, O6's part 3: our counterattack ordered with the covered division, as it reached the regiment; the battery covers it from the prepared place nearest the axis's point on the line, the axis from there to it.

rules.reason: The division goes forward: the regiment moves its batteries forward by bounds, one at a time.
rules.source: vr_1985_jurica_ad_on_the_move pp. 46-50 (air defence of troops on the move); vr_poltikovic_1984 p. 96 (the division's lines 6-8 km apart); voenizdat_osa_1991 pp. 232-239 (a battery changes position on the regiment commander's order); sam3d estimate (forward_m: a bound short of a line's 6 km; work_s, ready_in_s)
rules.notes: Track O, O6's part 3: the covered division's attack resumed or counterattack begun, as it reached the regiment, each once; the battery goes to the nearest prepared position a bound further forward.
